title: My live EA underperforms its backtest by ~20% and I've narrowed it to execution, not logic
author: socialwhizca
selftext:
Same EA, same parameters, MT5. Backtest on tick data shows a smooth curve, live has been running about 20% below expectancy over \~200 trades. Logic is identical so it's not a code divergence, I've traced most of the gap to two things: slippage on entry during fast moves, and the fact that my backtest assumed fills at prices that just weren't available live.

Currently live on AvaTrade. Before I go blaming the broker I want to rule out that my backtest was simply naive, no slippage model, no spread widening assumption, fills at ideal prices. My suspicion is that's 70% of the gap and execution venue is the other 30%.

For people who've actually A/B'd this: did you find execution quality varied enough between brokers to matter for a short-hold EA, or is the real lesson always "your backtest was lying to you"? Trying to figure out which lever to pull before I waste a month migrating brokers for a problem that was mine all along.

comments.author: WhisperingkrHid
comments.body:
Based on my experience, I’d be careful about blaming the broker alone. Backtests often look much better once you account for realistic spread changes, slippage, and imperfect fills.

I’ve seen similar gaps with short-hold strategies, and adding slippage assumptions narrowed the difference a lot. With only \~200 trades, I’d first compare the live execution logs to the backtest entries before switching brokers like Slickorps.
